claims.body: Since 2023-24, Kuemper has been shaky against the Senators, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.

story.head: Ice packs on standby
paras: The Kings won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Los Angeles on Oct 29. The Senators (14-6-3) lost 6-5 in overtime to Philadelphia on Thursday, while the Kings have won two in a row. Going in, the Kings are seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Sens third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Kings have played better than their record (.400) says: their chances are worth about .615, and their finishing has held them back. The Senators’ record (.674) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.603), largely because they’re 7-3 in one-goal games. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Senators (2nd) and the Kings (5th) both hound the puck on the forecheck. The Kings keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st) and leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest). As for the Senators, they rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it. Beyond that, good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Kings.

Adrian Kempe (6 G / 8 A / 14 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Kings’ scoring lead. Alex Laferriere (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 20 GP) shares it. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (11 G / 17 A / 28 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Drake Batherson (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.

Linus Ullmark (10-1-0 / .940 SV% in 11 GS) has been terrific for Ottawa and will likely start. Los Angeles has two options in net: Darcy Kuemper (7-5-1 / .885 SV% in 13 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-6-1 / .908 SV% in 7 GS). Kuemper has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Kuemper has a .837 save percentage in five starts against the Senators, well under his usual .904. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

The Senators are newly without Carter Yakemchuk, and have been without Warren Foegele, Jonas Johansson and William Eklund for several games. Linus Ullmark is expected to start.
Alex Laferriere has four goals on chances worth about 9.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
